headline: High: Flowise’s writable shared workspace and broad egress create default risks of leakage, prompt injection, and cascading mis-execution when paired with Authelia.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server files and run browser/API tools in flows, so attacker-controlled content can enter its graph and be forwarded. Authelia exposes OAuth2/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth outputs that Flowise could ingest as trusted inputs. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so injection is plausible in default deployments, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF Flowise flows ingest Authelia-generated headers, tokens, or file content without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace or uploaded file is used as an instruction channel, malicious content can steer downstream flow nodes.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to Authelia-derived inputs before Flowise consumes them.
Disable any flow node that interprets file or HTTP content as instructions.
Restrict Flowise file inputs to allowlisted paths only.
Review one representative flow for prompt-injection handling.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise explicitly touches chatflow inputs/outputs, server filesystem, uploaded files, and broad network egress; Authelia handles authentication traffic via OAuth2/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth. If Authelia artifacts or secrets are routed into Flowise, Flowise can transmit them to model providers or HTTP tools by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive auth material.
conditions: IF Authelia headers, tokens, or logs are stored in Flowise files or chatflow state, they can be read and forwarded.
IF a flow sends uploaded files or context to model providers or HTTP tools, those contents may leave the deployment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any Authelia-to-Flowise handoff.
Disable file upload nodes for flows handling auth data.
Use a separate Flowise instance for non-sensitive workloads.
Rotate any credentials that may have been exposed in shared state.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before model-provider calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OpenID-facing behavior, while Flowise has broad network egress plus writable filesystem access and shared server datastore state across instances. Even without shell or git writes, both can mutate shared mutable resources and external services, so overlapping writes can conflict in default deployments unless the operator adds isolation.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or datastore, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Flowise instances share server datastore state while Authelia updates related auth records externally, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different storage paths.
Use distinct service accounts and credentials.
Disable shared datastore access for unrelated Flowise instances.
Check for overlapping writes in one deployment run.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise’s graph-based tool nodes can treat upstream outputs as inputs, and Authelia emits authentication decisions and headers that may be consumed as authoritative. If Flowise chains those outputs into downstream actions or model prompts without verification, a mistaken auth result or malformed header can cascade into incorrect tool execution or user-facing decisions.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Authelia outputs as trusted routing or authorization signals, errors can propagate downstream.
IF a flow converts auth-related text into prompts or tool parameters without validation, one bad value can affect multiple nodes.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any downstream action node.
Log and inspect one end-to-end auth-to-flow path.
Mark Authelia outputs as untrusted in flow documentation.
Limit high-impact nodes to manually approved runs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between auth outputs and tool inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is that Flowise stores chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while Authelia is an auth service; without a documented mismatch, the pair shows only a small compliance gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated data through Flowise without a matching retention policy, compliance risk increases.
IF Authelia logs or secrets are retained in Flowise beyond policy, subject-rights or retention obligations may be affected.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for Flowise chatflow data.
Avoid placing regulated data in Flowise flows.
Document which auth artifacts may be stored.
Review one data-flow diagram for residency gaps.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
